result.topic_en: Riemann derives from the differential equations of shortest lines (geodesics) in new variables a set of conditions on the coefficients $a_{\iota\iota'}$ and their derivatives at the origin, and begins showing that a quadratic form identity forces its coefficients and their derivatives to vanish at the point 0.

$\sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\mu\iota}}{\partial x_{\iota'}} c_\iota c_{\iota'} = \frac12 \sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_\mu} c_\iota c_{\iota'}$

2

Aequationes differentiales linearum brevissimarum, ad novas variabiles relatae hae sunt:
[-$d \sum_\iota a_{\mu\iota} c_\iota$-]
$d \sum_\iota a_{\mu\iota} c_\iota = \frac12 dr \sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_\mu} c_\iota c_{\iota'}$
unde concludetur esse:
3. $\sum_{\iota\iota'} p_{\mu\iota\iota'} x_\iota x_{\iota'} = 0$
posito brevitatis causa:
$p_{\mu\iota\iota'} = \frac{\partial a_{\iota\mu}}{\partial x_{\iota'}} + \frac{\partial a_{\iota'\mu}}{\partial x_\iota} - \frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_\mu}$
sive [-z-]
3' $\sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota x_{\iota'} = 2 \sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\iota\mu}}{\partial x_{\iota'}} x_\iota x_{\iota'}$
Hae aequationes alia quadam forma exhiberi possunt. Ponatur brevitatis causa:
[-$\omega_\mu = \sum_\iota \frac{\partial a_{\mu\iota}}{\partial x}$-]
$\omega_\mu = \sum_\iota a_{\mu\iota} x_\iota$ ; $\frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} = a_{\mu\nu} + \sum_\iota \frac{\partial a_{\mu\iota}}{\partial x_\nu} x_\iota$
unde aequatio 3' formam induct:
$\omega_\mu + \sum_\iota \frac{\partial \omega_\iota}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota = 2 \sum_\iota \frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\iota} x_\iota$
Jam si ponitur
$2\omega = \sum_\iota \omega_\iota x_\iota$ , $2 \frac{\partial \omega}{\partial x_\mu} = \omega_\mu + \sum_\iota \frac{\partial \omega_\iota}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota$
ex hac aequatione sequitur:
$\frac{\partial \omega}{\partial x_\mu} = \sum_\iota \frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\iota} x_\iota$ ; $\frac{\partial \omega}{\partial x_\mu \partial x_\nu} = \frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} + \sum_\iota \frac{\partial^2 \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\iota \partial x_\nu} x_\iota$
unde:
$\frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} - \frac{\partial \omega_\nu}{\partial x_\mu} + \sum_\iota \frac{\partial}{\partial x_\iota} \left\{ \frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} - \frac{\partial \omega_\nu}{\partial x_\mu} \right\} x_\iota = 0$
Quae formula docet, $\frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} - \frac{\partial \omega_\nu}{\partial x_\mu}$ esse functionem homogeneam ordinis $-1$, quam per $f(x_1, x_2 \ldots x_n)$ designamus. Habemus itaque:
$f(tx_1, tx_2 \ldots tx_n) = t^{-1} f(x_1, x_2 \ldots x_n)$
unde concludimus, posito $t = 0$, si quidem supponimus, coefficientes $a_{\iota\iota'}$ earumque derivationes in puncto 0 habere valores determinatos finitos, functionem $f$ esse $= 0$, vel $\frac{\partial \omega_\mu}{\partial x_\nu} = \frac{\partial \omega_\nu}{\partial x_\mu}$, unde porro:
$\sum_\iota \frac{\partial a_{\mu\iota}}{\partial x_\nu} x_\iota = \sum_\iota \frac{\partial a_{\nu\iota}}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota$
quae aequationum 3' ope praebet:
$\sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\mu\iota}}{\partial x_{\iota'}} x_\iota x_{\iota'} = \sum_{\iota\iota'} \frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_\mu} x_\iota x_{\iota'} = 0$
et ope aequationum differentialium lineae brevissimae:
4. [-E-] $\sum_\iota a_{\mu\iota} c_\iota = \sum_\iota a^0_{\mu\iota} c_\iota$
Nunc si habetur aequatio formae:
$\sum_{\iota\iota'} t_{\iota\iota'} x_\iota x_{\iota'} = 0$
in qua $t_{\iota\iota'} = t_{\iota'\iota}$ sunt coefficientes [-quilibet-] {+quaelibet+}[?], qui simul cum [-derivationibus-] {+derivatis+}[?] primorum trium ordinum in puncto 0 habent valores determinatos finitos, sequitur, ter differentiando et posito $x_\iota = 0$:
$t_{\iota\iota'} = 0$ $\frac{\partial t_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}} + \frac{\partial t_{\iota'\iota''}}{\partial x_\iota} + \frac{\partial t_{\iota''\iota}}{\partial x_{\iota'}} = 0$
